correctness.rationale: The published CDF composed with x(t)=lambda sqrt(-2 log(1-exp(-t))) gives the Lomax survival since the transform is decreasing. The absolute Jacobian has log J(t)=-t/2+O(1) at infinity and log J(t)=-log t-(1/2)log log(1/t)+O(1) at zero. Under the Lomax density, -log f_T is absolutely integrable for all positive shapes, the positive part of log J is integrable, and its negative tail contributes asymptotically -(alpha beta^alpha/2)t^(-alpha) to the entropy integrand. Thus the change of variables is valid in the extended-real sense, including logarithmic divergence at alpha=1, with no subtraction of divergent expectations. Integrating the Lomax survival gives E[T]=beta/(alpha-1) for alpha>1, and log((beta+T)/beta) is exponential with rate alpha (the log-eta expectation is actually finite for every alpha>0). Differentiating the CDF and taking minus the log density yields exactly the simplified entropy formula; E[X^2] and E[|log X|] are finite in that regime by the same endpoint estimates. VERIFICATION.md and verify_entropy.py were inspected, not executed; the latter encodes formulas locally rather than checking a package API. The proof, not recorded or sampled output, establishes the boundary.
